motion.name: pour
motion.value: 2900ms; local picture yaw separated from stage-space tip; dock before departure; hold through final landing; loose intermittent gravity grains
motion.purpose: The in-progress revision places the mouth over the receiver after any inspection yaw. Falling grains accelerate downward with small spread. Existing static materials remain protected. This source-only merge does not verify the final pose or rendered flow.

motion.name: assembly
motion.value: 4000ms; frame tilt:28deg; affine frame projection; cumulative-area bank; departure:880–3240ms; mouth offset:60ms; last mouth:3300ms; last landing:3400ms; last settle:3440ms; accepted mesh handoff:3500ms; bottle return starts:3560ms
motion.purpose: Shrink and lift the frame before tilting. Preserve each clamped brushed position in a finite source bank whose capacity decreases monotonically toward the bottom-right outlet. Bridge the mat and wooden rim, then fall 26px into the upright mouth below. Hold both transfer poses through flow. One event schedule controls visible source, external stream, airborne interior and landed volume. Accumulate the accepted lit fine-grain treatment after landings, then restore the unchanged resting meshes, bottle pose and cork.

motion.name: rotation-release
motion.purpose: Decaying sealed-bottle pointer-release inertia; stops below .00005.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No CSS transitions or animations and no sealed release inertia. Both transfers reach their destination immediately. Manual loose push remains available, and restore is immediate.

motion.name: loose-push
motion.value: swept segment radius:28px; push=(1.7+min(1,length/14)*2.8)*falloff; linear damping:pow(.83,dt); no home spring
motion.purpose: Persistent grooves remain after motion settles, until explicit restore. Bitmap coordinates are independent of the bottle camera.

motion.name: loose-restore
motion.value: per-grain delay:0–140ms; duration:820ms; cubic ease:1-pow(1-t,3); final settling:980ms
motion.purpose: Explicitly gather grains back to their photo positions; reduced motion restores immediately.

materials.name: cork
materials.value: CanvasTexture base:#bd9567; MeshStandardMaterial color:0xffffff; bumpScale:.028; roughness:.96; envMapIntensity:.18
materials.purpose: Procedurally textured stopper and small top bevel.

materials.name: pixel-sand-field
materials.value: native Canvas2D:720×432; seeded LCG:907; sample interval:1.9px; jitter:1.7px; 85% 2×2 grains, otherwise 1×1; image-rendering:pixelated; warm luminance palette; background seeded LCG:412
materials.purpose: Loose play uses hard pixel grains with photo-derived warm colors, per-grain shade and a brighter top-left pixel over seeded brown gaps. The earliest cat demo guides this treatment. The same grains receive immutable routes from their actual brush positions. Pouring deposits at local impact points before downward and outward settling. Assembly clamps only to the finite native footprint, then drains a cumulative-area bank monotonically toward the low outlet; each grain remains visible until its own departure. Cancellation preserves brushed positions and completion restores the exact home picture. No projected WebGL plane renders the flat painting.

materials.name: photo-mantle
materials.value: 1536×~920 color and tangent-normal CanvasTextures; seeded LCG:173; irregular hull sides:5–7; local stretch:.92–1.08 before full-shape rotation:0–2PI; tilted crown and bevel faces; two-pass grain pitches:3.8px fine,7.4px larger; size=pitch*(minimum+pow(rand,.7)*variation), pass minimum/variation:(.38,.24),(.4,.28); crown peak:size*(.32–.44); rim height:size*.035; crown inset:.48–.64; shade:.91–1.13; local-color base:.84; contact-shadow target:.55, coverage:.24, offset:(.28,.4), blur:.35; MeshStandardMaterial color:0xbebebe; normalScale:(.9,.9); roughness:.94; metalness:0; envMapIntensity:.14; map and normalMap wrapS:RepeatWrapping, anisotropy:4; no bumpMap; material dispose owns normalMap.dispose; LatheGeometry radial segments:160; maximum radius:.966; y:-1.535 to 2.10; rotationY:PI
materials.purpose: Opaque packed sand follows the inner glass through shoulder and neck and receives lighting and shadows. Height-based UVs contain the photo once in the straight band from y=-1.49 to 1.20, preserving proportions against the actual circumference and height. Sand-colored support fills the remaining surface. Seam width is applied before the grain color and normal atlases. Compact fully rotated grains, fine underpacking and lower crowns replace the earlier coarse bodies. Each rasterized crown and bevel triangle supplies a sloped tangent-space normal without per-grain mesh geometry or grain collisions.

materials.name: packed-sand-cap
materials.value: 256×256 color and tangent-normal CanvasTextures over #bda17a; seeded LCG:173; irregular hull sides:5–7; local stretch:.92–1.08 before full-shape rotation:0–2PI; tilted crown and bevel faces; two-pass grain pitches:2.2px fine,4.0px larger; size=pitch*(minimum+pow(rand,.7)*variation), pass minimum/variation:(.38,.24),(.4,.28); crown peak:size*(.32–.44); rim height:size*.035; crown inset:.48–.64; shade:.91–1.13; local-color base:.84; contact-shadow target:.55, coverage:.24, offset:(.28,.4), blur:.35; MeshStandardMaterial color:0xbebebe; normalScale:(.9,.9); roughness:.94; metalness:0; envMapIntensity:.14; map and normalMap wrapS:RepeatWrapping, anisotropy:4; no bumpMap; material dispose owns normalMap.dispose; CircleGeometry radius:1; rotationX:-PI/2; scaled by sandRadiusAt(fillTop); y:2.10 at rest
materials.purpose: A sand-colored cap matches the accepted packed body, using compact fully rotated grain shapes, fine underpacking, lower crowns and tangent normals. The accepted static cap remains at y=2.10 and is hidden with the mantle during transfers. Assembly uses a private clone of its lit material and immutable textures on a separate temporary radial surface. The original body and cap return unchanged after the assembly handoff. Their opaque resting volume has no dark core.

materials.name: plinth
materials.purpose: Low cylindrical display base and shadow receiver.

materials.name: moving-sand-interior
materials.value: pour: unchanged transient THREE.Points ShaderMaterial and compact shaded sprites; assembly: private MeshStandardMaterial clones sharing accepted immutable color/normal textures and side geometry; landed-volume lookup:1024 levels; temporary cap:24 rings×96 sectors; cone amplitude<=.15; radial ripple multiplier:.06; sparse airborne point limits:.45–1.2px
materials.purpose: The pour keeps its temporary point volume with an independent whole-bottle tip and loose packet-based gravity stream. Assembly accumulates opaque lit fine-grain sand using actual landing times and an inner-profile volume lookup. A temporary low conical top with small ripples tapers flat near full volume. Only grains from mouth crossing until landing use small airborne points. Temporary meshes own cloned materials and cap geometry. Accepted textures and side geometry remain shared and unchanged. The resting renderer is never retuned. These are authored bounds and mass events without grain collisions.

materials.name: mouth-grain-stream
materials.value: transparent Canvas2D overlay; DPR capped at 2; route samples from the native grain plan; affine frame origin and axes; explicit outer-rim lip; gravity fall during assembly; downward accelerating pour; warm bodies and top-left highlights
materials.purpose: The pour replaces target-seeking cubic paths with a loose intermittent gravity grains beneath the mouth. Assembly starts each grain at the tilted native outlet after its own departure, crosses the mat and wooden rim, then falls through the actual mouth below 60ms later. The outlet and mouth hold their poses during assembly flow. Source departure, external stream, airborne interior and settled bottle volume share one event schedule. Stream resources clear after transfer. Paths are authored without grain collisions.

provenance.authority: The cat grain reference and earliest interactive demo guide loose play. Smithsonian and Petra photographs guide packed sand, filled profile and perspective. The code-led world remains direction seed 889eefe6, candidate 5, personal display plinth. User acceptance "瓶子的效果可以了" protects the warm sealed material, geometry, camera, glass, lighting and rotation. The user rejected the clipped sand block, upward assembly suction, then a prematurely empty frame and mismatched transient bottle sand. The current finite-bank schedule and cloned lit assembly materials address the latest feedback. These corrections are authorized but not user-accepted; an internal review does not establish that acceptance.
provenance.tonalRamps: Synthesized OKLCH display metadata with source hue/chroma; these are not additional implemented color tokens.
provenance.notCanonized: The clipped photographic plug, broad frame reveal, upward assembly suction, prematurely collapsed source bank and sparse point-cloud appearance for settled assembly sand were rejected by the user and are not design rules. Rotation buttons, seam disclosure, the push/swirl switch and the footer are removed from the current interface. Decorative slogans, repeated instructions, stage narration and permanent save-success copy remain removed. The downward-pour revision has actual three-width sequential captures. Internal verification does not establish user acceptance.
provenance.currentDemo: src/main.ts uses the bundled src/assets/cat.png illustration; this source image is demonstration content, not a reusable design-system rule.
provenance.reviewEvidence: Frozen bundle index-BO10qENP.js has actual desktop1440, mobile390, user590 and flat718 captures, eight pour phases and a26s normal-speed recording. Fresh internal finish disposition: ship. Motion review used recording/sequence samples, not raw MP4 playback. Static front and rotated PNG comparisons are exact. These checks do not establish user acceptance.

narrative.northStar: A personal display plinth in warm daylight
narrative.overview:
A quiet personal display plinth in warm daylight is the implementation’s working visual metaphor. Warm paper, brown ink and restrained terracotta controls frame the photograph as a small object to keep. The photograph supplies the tonal structure of the warm sand; the surrounding interface stays low in chroma.

This system records the built application. The user-provided cat grain reference and earliest interactive demo guide loose play. The Smithsonian and Petra photographs in [Visual references](docs/visual-references.md) guide packed sand, the filled profile and perspective. Direction seed (889eefe6), grounded candidate 5, remains the code-led personal display plinth. The user accepted the fine-grain bottle with "瓶子的效果可以了". That acceptance protects the warm sealed material, geometry, camera, glass, lighting and rotation.

The user subsequently rejected the rigid sand block disappearing during pouring and requested fine grains leaving the bottle, landing and spreading in the frame. That direction uses one route schedule across the interior, stream and flat painting. The user then rejected upward suction during assembly and requested a tilted frame pouring into a bottle below. Earlier assembly feedback rejects a frame that appears empty while the bottle continues filling, and the temporary bottle sand texture. Assembly now drains a finite source bank through the low corner on a cumulative-area schedule; its settled bottle volume uses private clones of the accepted lit fine-grain materials. Only airborne assembly grains use particles. The current interface keeps the exact headline "把回忆装进沙子里" and one bottom-center gesture hint. Rotation buttons, seam controls, the push/swirl switch and the footer are removed. The downward-pour pose separates photo yaw from the bottle tip, docks before grain departure and holds through the final landing. These changes have not received user acceptance, and an internal review does not establish that acceptance. The name 砂藏 / Sandkeep remains provisional. Reflective glass, textured cork, faceted packed sand and a contact shadow describe the rendering without a photorealism claim.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, low-chroma interface around a photograph rendered as warm sand.
Chinese serif display type paired with Chinese system sans controls.
One workbench with photo selection and the primary switch above the art, one gesture hint inside it, restore beside the primary action, and a quiet reset below.
Restrained interface depth; soft lift belongs to the picture frame and material depth to the 3D object.

A shared grain schedule connects the temporary bottle interior, bottle-mouth stream and local deposits in the frame. Assembly drains a finite bank from a tilted frame. The pour holds the mouth above loose intermittent downward grains after any inspection yaw.

rules.name: The Warm Sand Rule
rules.body: Let the photograph supply the tonal structure of the warm sand. Use clay for the principal action, focus and small identity accents.

rules.name: The Two Type Voices Rule
rules.body: Use the bundled serif for the product name and main headline; use the system sans stack for controls and supporting copy.

rules.name: The Object Depth Rule
rules.body: Keep ordinary controls flat; reserve soft elevation for the physical picture frame and material depth for the bottle, cork, grains, plinth and scene contact shadow.

dos: Do use the existing paper, ink, muted, line, clay and stage roles instead of introducing parallel surface colors.
Do preserve the bundled serif headline and system sans control relationship.
Do keep interactive targets at least the observed 44px height, with the existing clay focus treatment.
Do place photo selection and the primary switch above the art, with one state-specific gesture hint inside its bottom center, restore next to the main switch and a quiet reset below.
Do retain one scene height through each ready and transfer state at the active breakpoint.
Do preserve the finished photograph while turning the bottle and respect reduced motion.
Do hold the tilted frame outlet above the actual mouth during assembly, then return the bottle to its accepted resting renderer after the last grain settles.
donts: Don't extend the picture frame’s soft shadow into ordinary controls or introduce rounded floating panels.
Don't reintroduce naming or an original-color selector into this workflow.
Don't blur the loose field's hard pixel grains, top-left highlights or dark gaps.
Don't copy the loose field's dark gaps onto packed sand. Keep packed grain variation near its local photo color.
Don't alter the accepted warm sealed renderer to tune loose play or transient transfer poses.
Don't drain a clipped photographic block or reveal the whole frame independently of grain landings.
Don't pull assembly grains upward from the frame or add a tilt over the old suction path.
Don't hide the source bank before its scheduled departures or render settled assembly sand as a sparse point cloud.
Don't treat the earlier bottle acceptance as approval of the new interface or transfer sequence, or claim photorealism from the reference photographs.
